newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss pick WJC leader Bronfman for Holocaust panel.
newsitem.headline: Swiss pick WJC leader Bronfman for Holocaust panel.

text.p: Switzerland has elected World Jewish Congress (WJC) President Edgar Bronfman as a member of the panel administering a memorial fund for Holocaust victims, the government said in a statement on Wednesday.

Bronfman replaces Nobel Prize winning author Elie Wiesel, who was nominated to the seven-member board but then declined to to take up the post of chairman for the 265 million Swiss franc ($186.4 million) fund financed by Swiss banks and private businesses.

Bronfman has led the WJC's fight over unclaimed Jewish assets in Switzerland. Jewish organisation have accused Swiss banks of hoarding billions of dollars in dormant wealth of Holocaust victims, which banks deny.

Wiesel resigned from the fund's board earlier this month, citing statements "made in the Swiss press" and after Swiss officials made clear his title of international chairman carried no special powers. WJC officials said this had insulted Wiesel.

Four of the fund's members are named by the Swiss government and three by the World Jewish Restitution Organisation, a branch of the WJC. WJC Executive Director Elan Steinberg has said Bronfman will serve only until a permanent replacement is found.

"The Federal Council (cabinet) now hopes that the Special Fund in support of needy Holocaust victims, who are elderly, can soon take up its work," the statement said, adding Berne had also elected 18 members of the fund's advisory council.
